module_summary: modules/bdm/src is the fork-vendored ps2sdk Block Device Manager (bdm.irx, ps2.yaml target bdm_drv): a mount table that pairs block devices with filesystem drivers on a 4 KB event thread, plus MBR/GPT partition drivers that publish pseudo block devices; RiptOPL changes add a 512-byte sector gate, partition I/O bounds and a gap-tolerant GPT scan. modules/bdmassault/ilink_bd_assault is a separate make-built IRX (only built by the flavours.yml popstarter-ilink-driver job) that links an older copy of ps2sdk's iLinkman (i.LINK link-layer manager: PHY, UBUF/PHT transmit, interrupt and request handlers, configuration ROM) and IEEE1394_bd (SBP-2 login/ORB transport plus a SCSI block layer that registers with BDM) into one module, shipped as POPSTARTER's usbhdfsd.irx.ilink. It is a near copy of modules/ilink/iLinkman and modules/ilink/IEEE1394_bd, differing in a cdvdman-free GetConsoleIDs, a chained _start, an older bdm.h without the path field, no READ(16) path and no device-number fix.

reusable_helpers.what: splits a u64 into two u32 for printf

findings.title: ilink_bd_assault carries a second, drifting copy of iLinkman and IEEE1394_bd (about 3,500 lines) instead of building from modules/ilink
findings.problem: Every file under ilink_bd_assault/src/{IEEE1394_bd,iLinkman} is a near copy of modules/ilink: iLink_intr/TxRx/DMA/PHY differ only in the include path, iLink.c only in the chained BD_iLink_start call, sbp2_driver.c by 57 diff lines (it lacks sbp2FreeDevNr), scsi.c is the older SDK one (no READ(16), 12-byte CDB). ORIGIN.txt:18-20 says 'A change to one belongs in both', and the #1024 and October 22 fixes were applied twice; the copies already drift.
findings.fix: Build ilink_bd_assault.irx from modules/ilink/iLinkman/src and modules/ilink/IEEE1394_bd/src with one define (for example ILINK_BD_ASSAULT) that selects the static GetConsoleIDs, the chained _start/BD_iLink_start and no IRX_ID in IEEE1394_bd main.c, the malloc/free single definition, and skips bd->path for the older include/bdm.h; keep only Makefile, include/bdm.h, src/imports.lst and src/exports.tab here, then delete the copied trees and point the dual-copy tests at one source.
findings.justification: Adds roughly 30-40 lines of #ifdef in modules/ilink to remove about 3,500 duplicated lines; it ends the double maintenance that ORIGIN.txt documents and gives the POPSTARTER build the fixes it is missing (device-number, READ(16) for disks past 2 TiB).
findings.benefit: ~3,500 source lines removed (sum of the cited bdmassault files 3,515 plus iLink_internal.h/iLink_CROM.h, minus ~40 ifdef lines); every future i.LINK fix made once. No menu ELF change claimed. INFERRED.
findings.evidence: Python difflib and diff -w between each bdmassault file and modules/ilink: iLink_intr.c, iLink_TxRx.c, iLink_DMA.c, iLink_PHY.c only include-path and one comment differ; iLink.c differs at :74,:160-163 (BD_iLink_start chain); iLink_internal.c at GetConsoleIDs :57-64, dmac_enable vs sceEnableDMAChannel, malloc ifdef :170-191; iLink_crom.c older endian handling; sbp2_driver.c diff 57 lines incl. missing sbp2FreeDevNr (modules/ilink sbp2_driver.c:403-427); scsi.c 141 diff lines (no READ_16/READ_CAPACITY_16). include/bdm.h lacks the path field that modules/ilink scsi.c sets. INFERRED part: the pinned PS2DEVPINNED container used by flavours.yml:363-398 must accept the shared source (e.g. sceEnableDMAChannel names); console testing required.

findings.title: Five per-component import/export files inside ilink_bd_assault are never used by its Makefile
findings.problem: The Makefile sets IOP_SRC_DIR := src/, so imports.o/exports.o come from src/imports.lst and src/exports.tab with src/irx_imports.h; no .c file includes irx_imports.h. The sub-tree copies are leftovers: IEEE1394_bd/src/imports.lst lacks I_PollEventFlag that sbp2_driver.c:392 calls, and iLinkman/src/imports.lst:1-4 still imports cdvdman sceCdRI/sceCdRM, which README.md says would abort loading under POPSTARTER.
findings.fix: Delete the five files (independently of finding 1).
findings.benefit: 244 lines and 5 stray files removed (73+35+30+74+32); no binary change. Removes a misleading cdvdman import list. INFERRED (standard PS2SDK Makefile.iopglobal rules, not in repo).
findings.evidence: Makefile:9,13-14 IOP_OBJS = exports.o ... imports.o, IOP_SRC_DIR := src/; custom rules :31-36 only compile .c. git grep '#include' over ilink_bd_assault/src: no source includes irx_imports.h. Grep cdvdman: only iLinkman/src/imports.lst:1-4 imports it. Grep test_ilink*.py for imports.lst/exports.tab/irx_imports: no hits. PollEventFlag absent from IEEE1394_bd/src/imports.lst but present in src/imports.lst:64.

findings.title: Never-enabled debug blocks (REQ_CHECK_DMAC_STAT, REQ_CHECK_ERRORS) and commented-out code in both iLinkman copies
findings.problem: REQ_CHECK_DMAC_STAT and REQ_CHECK_ERRORS are only commented-out #defines in iLink_internal.h:17-18 and appear in no Makefile, ps2.yaml or test, so the DMAC stall-recovery and HdrErr/SntBsyAck blocks never compile; the same file pair also keeps commented-out code (old ctrl0 setup, PHY config handling, ack test).
findings.fix: Delete the #ifdef REQ_CHECK_DMAC_STAT / REQ_CHECK_ERRORS blocks, their two commented #defines and the commented-out code lines, in both copies (once, if finding 1 merges them).
findings.benefit: ~50 lines per copy, ~100 in total; no binary change (code is not compiled). INFERRED.
findings.evidence: git grep -n REQ_CHECK_DMAC_STAT/REQ_CHECK_ERRORS over the repo (excluding docs): only the #ifdef sites in both iLinkman copies and the commented defines at iLink_internal.h:17-18 (both copies); Makefile:10 defines only REQ_CHECK_CONSOLE_VERSION; ps2.yaml iLinkman_fork (:319-326) defines nothing. DEBUG_TTY_FEEDBACK is kept: test_ilink_manager_recovery.py:149 builds with it.

findings.title: Dead USE_CUSTOM_ILINKMAN_MALLOC_AND_FREE block duplicates sbp2_driver.c malloc/free
findings.problem: USE_CUSTOM_ILINKMAN_MALLOC_AND_FREE is defined nowhere, so the iLinkman malloc/free copy never compiles; the combined module uses the identical pair in sbp2_driver.c:782-801 (the #ifdef exists only to avoid duplicate symbols).
findings.benefit: 22 lines removed; no binary change. INFERRED.
findings.evidence: git grep -n USE_CUSTOM_ILINKMAN_MALLOC_AND_FREE: only iLink_internal.c:170. modules/ilink copy has the functions unconditional (separate iLinkman.irx). Bodies compared line by line with sbp2_driver.c:782-801.

findings.title: Unused pieces in both SBP-2 drivers: DeinitIEEE1394, the get_max_lun hook, the always-LOGIN mode parameter, stray include and comments
findings.problem: DeinitIEEE1394 has no caller (only its prototype) and is the only reader that needs iLinkIntrCBThreadID global; sbp2_get_max_lun always returns 0 and scsi_warmup only M_DEBUGs it; ieee1394_SendManagementORB is only called with SBP2_LOGIN_REQUEST and rejects anything else; usbhdfsd-common.h supplies nothing used; a commented-out declaration and IRX_ID remain.
findings.fix: Delete DeinitIEEE1394 and its prototype and make iLinkIntrCBThreadID a local; delete sbp2_get_max_lun, the get_max_lun member and its call; drop the mode parameter (always LOGIN) and its guard; drop the usbhdfsd-common.h include and the commented lines. Adjust the tests that extract these functions by signature (test_ilink_sbp2_completion.py, test_ilink_bd_reset.py, test_ilink_bd_assault_reset.py, test_ilink_scsi_geometry.py).
findings.benefit: ~25 lines per copy, ~50 total; DeinitIEEE1394 and sbp2_get_max_lun are non-static or referenced, so a few dozen bytes per IRX (INFERRED, not measured).
findings.evidence: git grep DeinitIEEE1394: definitions sbp2_driver.c:775 (bdmassault) and :802 (ilink), prototypes sbp2_disk.h:180 (both), no caller, not in any exports.tab. ieee1394_SendManagementORB callers: sbp2_driver.c:250 only, with SBP2_LOGIN_REQUEST (tests also pass LOGIN). get_max_lun: set at sbp2_driver.c:87, called only at scsi.c:170 (result only logged), same in modules/ilink scsi.c:215-216. sbp2_driver.c uses no USBMASS_/bd_fragment symbol.

findings.title: scsi_read and scsi_write are the same loop in both IEEE1394_bd copies
findings.problem: scsi_read and scsi_write differ only in the const qualifier and the write flag passed to scsi_cmd_rw_sector; the 25-line chunking/retry loop is written twice in each copy.
findings.fix: Keep one static scsi_rw(bd, sector, buffer, count, write) with the loop and make scsi_read/scsi_write one-line calls (or point the block_device read/write at thin wrappers).
findings.benefit: ~20 lines per copy, ~40 total; roughly 100-150 bytes of IRX code per copy (INFERRED: one fewer copy of a small loop).
findings.evidence: Read bdmassault scsi.c:238-263 vs :265-290 side by side: identical apart from 'const' and the 0/1 argument; modules/ilink scsi.c:304 and :332 same pattern (diff with bdmassault shows only the debug macro lines differ).

findings.title: scsiCommandBudget re-implements sbp2ElapsedUs, and the TEST UNIT READY try count duplicates the 30 s budget
findings.problem: scsi.c:36-41 repeats sbp2ElapsedUs's GetSystemTime/64-bit subtract/SysClock2USec sequence from the same module. The warm-up is bounded twice: SCSI_READY_TRIES 300 polls at 100 ms each cannot end before about 30 s, which is SCSI_READY_BUDGET_US, the elapsed bound checked in the same condition.
findings.fix: Make sbp2ElapsedUs non-static (declare it in scsi.h) and call it from scsiCommandBudget; drop SCSI_READY_TRIES and the tries counter, keeping the elapsed-time budget.
findings.benefit: ~10 lines per copy, ~20 total; small code-size saving (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Compared scsi.c:30-41 with sbp2_driver.c:145-154: same statements. scsi.c:186 checks '++tries >= SCSI_READY_TRIES || !scsiCommandBudget(scsi)', with DelayThread(SCSI_READY_RETRY_US = 100 ms) per iteration and budget 30 s. Tests (test_ilink_bd_assault_reset.py) compile scsi.c with sbp2ElapsedUs 'when present', so the shared helper must be provided to them.

findings.title: POPSTARTER i.LINK driver registers the full iLinkman export table that nothing imports
findings.problem: The combined module links IEEE1394_bd statically to iLinkman, yet still exports 22 iLinkman entry points and calls RegisterLibraryEntries. Under POPSTARTER the only other driver is bdm_assault (usbd.irx.ilink), so nothing imports them; iLinkAddCROMUnit/DeleteCROMUnit, GetNodeCapabilities, SetNodeCapabilities, DisableSBus and GetLocalNodeEUI64 are reachable only through this table and stay in a memory-card IRX.
findings.fix: Reduce src/exports.tab to the mandatory _start/_exit/_retonly slots (or drop the library registration) and let the export-only functions be removed; verify on a console that POPSTARTER loads the module without the iLinkman library.
findings.benefit: Export-only functions are ~70 lines of C (cited ranges); a few hundred bytes of the 27,769-byte usbhdfsd.irx.ilink (INFERRED, not measured).
findings.evidence: sbp2_driver.c calls only iLinkEnableSBus, SetTrCallbackHandler, GetGenerationNumber, GetLocalNodeID, GetNodeCount, TrAlloc, TrFree, TrWrite, GetNodeMaxSpeed, GetNodeTrSpeed, FindUnit, ReadCROM (read in full). PROVENANCE.md: usbd.irx.ilink is bdm_assault.irx (byte-identical to usbexfat). INFERRED: that POPSTARTER/bdm_assault never import iLinkman, and that the export removal frees bytes (dropping unreferenced functions needs --gc-sections, not confirmed for this Makefile build). README.md item 4 notes iopfixup needs exports.o first, so keep a minimal table.

findings.title: ilink_bd_assault build leftovers: redundant -DREQ_CHECK_CONSOLE_VERSION, empty IOP_LIB, cdvdman.h includes
findings.problem: REQ_CHECK_CONSOLE_VERSION is already #defined unconditionally in iLink_internal.h:16 (included by iLink.c before its use), so the Makefile -D only duplicates it; IOP_LIB is never set and IOP_INC_DIR names src/include/, which does not exist; iLink_internal.c still includes cdvdman.h although GetConsoleIDs no longer calls cdvdman, and SIF_CALLBACKS_12_13 is never defined.
findings.fix: Drop the -DREQ_CHECK_CONSOLE_VERSION flag, the $(IOP_LIB) references and IOP_INC_DIR, the cdvdman.h include in iLink_internal.c and the SIF_CALLBACKS_12_13 guard.
findings.benefit: ~6 lines; no binary change expected (INFERRED; the CI byte check in flavours.yml:376-391 would confirm).
findings.evidence: git grep REQ_CHECK_CONSOLE_VERSION: Makefile:10, iLink_internal.h:16 (#define), iLink.c:60,88 (after #include at :23). ls src: no include/ directory. git grep SIF_CALLBACKS_12_13: only #ifdef sites. iLink_internal.c:57-64 uses no cdvdman symbol.

findings.title: GPT driver re-checks a sector size that bdm_try_mount already guarantees to be 512
findings.problem: part_connect_gpt is reached only through g_gpt_fs.connect_bd, which bdm_try_mount calls only after refusing every device whose sectorSize != 512, so entriesPerSector is always 4 and the entriesPerSector <= 0 branch (added in commit 5fe47865, not SDK code) cannot run.
findings.benefit: 6 lines; a few instructions in bdm.irx (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: part_driver.c:140 is the only assignment of part_connect_gpt (g_gpt_fs.connect_bd); fs connect_bd is only called at bdm.c:184, after the sectorSize != 512 return at :169-180. Partition pseudo devices copy bd->sectorSize (part_driver_gpt.c:171), so they also pass the gate only at 512. git blame: lines 69-74 from 5fe47865 (2026-10-27).

findings.title: Upstream BDM leftovers: always-true MBR 'valid' counter, unused GPT GUID and attribute macros, unneeded includes
findings.problem: In partitions_sanity_check_mbr 'valid' is incremented on every loop pass and the loop either returns early or ends with valid == 4, so 'valid == 4' is always true; MS_BASIC_DATA_PARTITION_GUID and the GPT_PART_ATTR_PLATFORM_REQUIRED/LEGACY_BOOTABLE/TYPE_* and GPT_BDP_ATTR_* macros are referenced nowhere; part_driver.c includes mbr_types.h, gpt_types.h, errno.h and string.h without using them.
findings.fix: Return active > 0 and delete the valid counter; delete the unused GUID and macros; drop the four unused includes from part_driver.c. Upstream ps2sdk code: optional, or offer upstream.
findings.benefit: ~15 lines; no binary change (static const arrays and macros are not emitted when unused). INFERRED.
findings.evidence: git grep MS_BASIC_DATA_PARTITION_GUID, GPT_BDP_, GPT_PART_ATTR_ over the repo: only gpt_types.h definitions, plus GPT_PART_ATTR_IGNORE used at part_driver_gpt.c:153 (kept). part_driver.c uses only part_driver.h, stdio (via M_ macros) and bdm.h symbols. part_driver_mbr.c:19-30 read: valid++ unconditional at :29.
